kind: Post-download visual feasibility review only; all32 source contact sheets plus tagcrop sheets0/3, not a new accuracy benchmark or biological identity labeling. No OCR/detector calls.
observations: Most frontal feeding-barrier images make an ear tag physically attributable to a nearby head by visible attachment. Dense heads, rails, cropped/occluded bodies and edge-on tags require explicit ambiguity; nearest bodybox is not certified ownership.

Some native4000-pixel images show legible handwritten longnumbers mixed with short herd/date lines. This does not certify a legal identifier scheme. No country labels or valid-checkdigit guarantee are published.

The640x368 imagegroup has10–23pixel tag boxes, where source text is not recoverably legible in the displayed nativecrops. Several1440x1080examples also show substantial motionblur/interlacing despite adequate rectangle size.
At least one native4000-pixel image gives two tag views from one visible cow, useful for within-frame attachment consistency. Such correlated views are not independent temporal confirmations.

The published rectangles do not supply biologicalcowID, tagtranscript, cowbodyinstances or video/temporalgrouping. No sourcefilename order was used as timing. Three missingTXTfiles retained explicitly as unannotated, not emptynegative truth.
CEGD-R and CEID-D derive from the same authorcollection. Potential source/cowoverlap must be resolved before claiming independent OCRgeneralization on fullframes.
next_distinct_question: A frozen, independently reviewed tag-to-head/body ownership sample with completevisible animal instances and literaltext uncertainty could test same-animal binding. It cannot establish repeated-frame reliability without sourcevideo provenance. Keep OCRnumber proposals reversible and do not automatically merge anonymous cowprofiles from generic confidence alone.
